meta.title: Mandarin Chinese — Character parts for Level 1
meta.subtitle: The 42 parts Level 1's characters share — beside Level 1
meta.desc: The 42 parts that Level 1's characters are most often written from, one card each: every part found in at least 3 of the 248 characters on Level 1's fronts, counting a character where its Level 1 card splits it into two parts or more. 173 of those 248 characters contain at least one of them, so a character met for the first time is rarely all new. The front shows the part; the back gives its reading and meaning, how many Level 1 characters use it, and up to 6 of them, each with the first Level 1 word it is written in, that word's reading and meaning, and a speaker. THE ORDER is the order Level 1 first needs them: a part stands where the first word written with it stands in the Level 1 deck, so studied a few cards a day beside that deck it arrives before, or with, its first character. At the default of ten new cards a day the deck takes 5 days. — WHAT IS NOT HERE: stroke order, and the 164 parts found in only one or two Level 1 characters, which the Level 1 cards themselves show. A part is listed as the Level 1 cards break their characters down, one level deep. — Parts, their readings and meanings: Make Me a Hanzi, as carried on the HSK 3.0 Level 1 cards. Words, readings and meanings: the HSK 3.0 Level 1 deck on this shelf (the official HSK 3.0 vocabulary lists, and CC-CEDICT, CC BY-SA 4.0).
